title: chat v1: introduce framed-JSON streaming envelopes, stop-token reconciliation, and function-call metadata passthrough for /v1/chat parity
author: Maya Torres
release_notes: Add a framed JSON envelope for chat streaming to improve resilience and make /v1/chat compatible with structured outputs and function-call metadata. Stop-token reconciliation updated to align behavior with OpenAI stop arrays; logprobs moved to a separate metadata envelope during streaming. Backwards-compatible: legacy clients still supported by opt-in header. This PR adds an opt-in header "X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-v1" to preserve the pre-existing newline-delimited protocol for older clients and allow staged rollouts.
description: Motivation: We have multiple incompatibilities between our internal streaming protocol and the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions streaming expectations that surface as flaky tool/function-calling handshakes, ambiguous stop-token semantics, and broken partial-logprob delivery for structured outputs. This PR: 1) introduces a lightweight 'framed JSON' envelope for every stream fragment (type + seq + payload) so consumers can reliably reassemble partial JSON structured outputs and function call metadata, 2) reconciles stop-token handling when callers provide an array of stop strings by prioritizing exact-token termination while preserving internal role-based stop heuristics, and 3) moves per-chunk logprob deltas into a dedicated metadata envelope so streaming parsers don't get malformed JSON when logprobs are emitted mid-response. Summary of changes: - runtime/stream/framer.go: new envelope encoder/decoder and heartbeat handling (adds sequence numbers, fragment_type field). - api/openai/v1_adapter.go: map OpenAI chat params -> internal request shape; implement stop-array reconciliation logic and add compatibility header opt-in for legacy behavior. - server/handler/chat_stream_handler.go: emit framed JSON chunks, ensure function-call partials include "fc_meta" header with call_id & arg_fragment indices, add backoff on transient write failures to reduce partial chunk loss. - sdk/ts/openai_compat.ts: client-side helpers to decode framed stream and rehydrate function-call arguments into a final call object. - docs/openai_compat.md: compatibility notes and migration guide. - tests/integration/chat_stream_stop_test.go: synthetic scenarios covering overlapping stops, multi-stop arrays, and streaming logprob envelopes. Backcompat and rollout: default behavior for new streams will be the framed JSON envelope. We add an opt-in header "X-Redwood-Compat: legacy-v1" to preserve the pre-existing newline-delimited protocol for older clients. This allows staged rollouts. Implementation details: - Framed JSON envelope schema (per-line): {"type":"chunk|meta|heartbeat|eof","seq":int,"payload":<object|string>} where payload for "chunk" contains {"role","content_fragment"} or for functioncall partials {"fc_meta": {"call_id","index"}, "args_fragment"}. - Stop reconciliation: when client supplies stop: [s1,s2,...] we perform longest-prefix match first, then exact token match, then fallback to role-based internal stops. We also expose an explicit boolean flag "openai_stop_strict" on the internal request if caller expects strict array semantics. - Logprobs: emitted as {"type":"meta","seq":N,"payload":{"event":"logprobs","deltas":{...}}} to avoid injecting numeric arrays into text fragments. Tests: unit tests for the framer encoder/decoder, integration tests that run a simulated slow backend to validate sequence reordering recovery and heartbeats, and CI flakiness checks. Migration notes for SDKs: TS SDK adds decodeFramedStream helper and examples in quickstarts. Rollout plan: feature gated behind feature flag "framed_stream_v1" for two weeks, then enabled by default with opt-out header. CI: some early runs failed due to race in framer when seq overflowed in the simulated test; fixed in commit "avoid seq reuse on late reconnect". Known limitations: this change increases request/response byte counts slightly due to framing fields; we mitigate with compact encoding (short keys) and optional compression in Dedicated. Related issues: SUP-4421 (customer reported malformed structured output on streaming), ENG-1327 (spec alignment work).
